I'm applying for the Full Stack Software Engineer II role.

I've been a Morning Brew reader for years. The newsletter does what good content should do—it respects your time and makes you smarter. I inspected morningbrew.com before applying—Next.js, solid Lighthouse scores (92% performance, 96% best practices), though I noticed about 20 React hydration errors (#418) in the console. SSR/CSR mismatches are tricky; I've debugged similar issues in my own Next.js work. The site is well-built, and I'd love to help make it even better.

Your stack is my stack. Next.js, React, TypeScript—that's what I use every day. Postgres, Vercel, Cloudflare—I've built production systems on all three. At Webflow, I built a Dashboard (SvelteKit, similar React patterns) that creators use daily, an App Submission Form (Next.js, PostgreSQL) with complete user flows, and a Validator that checks templates against best practices.

You want someone with a high level of ownership who ships quickly. That's how I work. When the Marketplace team needed a submission system, I didn't wait for specs—I built it. When Support needed an LMS, I built it. When templates needed validation, I built a Designer Extension from scratch. I see problems, I propose solutions, I ship.

I also understand the content side. I spent a year as an On-Screen Educator at Webflow, creating tutorials and curriculum. I know what it takes to make content that resonates—and I know how engineering can make that content easier to create, distribute, and consume.

I don't have Go experience, but I've shipped Rust to production and I pick up languages when the work requires it. Python is what I use for AI work on the side.

Morning Brew built trust by respecting its audience. I'd love to help build the tools that keep that trust going.

P.S. Dan Toomey is my hero.

— Micah Johnson
